thread.title: Facebook, Alphabet defy stock market dip as Apple, other Silicon Valley stocks fall

author: Marlize van Romburgh
title: Facebook, Alphabet defy stock market dip as Apple, other Silicon Valley stocks fall
text: – Assistant Managing Editor for Digital, Silicon Valley Business Journal Feb 21, 2018, 1:38pm PST Updated Feb 21, 2018, 2:54pm PST Silicon Valley stocks were dragged down by a general slide in U.S. equities on Wednesday. Bloomberg's Silicon Valley High Tech index closed down 0.32 percent as 10 of its 13 members sank. The decline among local stocks mirrored the broader markets, with the Dow Jones Industrial Average down 167 points and the S&P 500 slipping 0.55 percent. Investors were rattled by new indications that the Fed plans to hike interest rates — albeit gradually — as a counterbalance against economic growth and rising inflation. Three stocks on the Bloomberg index — Facebook (NASAQ: FB), Alphabet (NASDAQ: GOOG) and Symantec (NASDAQ: SYMC) — defied the sell-off and closed higher. The rest, including the index's biggest stock, Apple (NASDAQ: AAPL), posted declines. The worst performers on the index were Advanced Micro Devices (NASDAQ: AMD), Cisco Systems (NASDAQ: CSCO), Juniper Networks (NYSE: JNPR), HP Inc (NYSE: HPQ) , Applied Materials (NASDAQ: AMAT) and Oracle Corp. (NASDAQ: ORCL). Among all Silicon Valley stocks, the worst performers were: Arista Networks (NYSE: ANET) dropped 4.65 percent. The stock started sliding last week after earnings hinted that an ongoing patent dispute with larger rival Cisco Systems could hurt sales. Super Micro Computer (NASDAQ: SMCI) sank 3.71 percent. Nvidia Corp. (NASDAQ: NVDA) fell 3.04 percent. Equinix (NASDAQ: EQIX) closed down 2.91 percent. Along with Synaptics , up 1.1 percent, and Facebook , up 1.08 percent, the best performers among Silicon Valley stocks were: Shutterfly (NASDAQ: SFLY) gained 1.69 percent. Silicon Valley Bank parent SVB Financial Group (NASDAQ: SIVB) popped 1.27 percent. Palo Alto Networks (NYSE: PANW) gained 0.91 percent. – Assistant Managing Editor for Digital, Silicon Valley Business Journal Feb 21, 2018, 1:38pm PST Updated Feb 21, 2018, 2:54pm PST Related Content
